grooves.name: afrobeats
grooves.description: afrobeats: Naija afropop pocket; kick on 1, the and of 2 and 3 (a push on the and of 4 in bar 2), rim on the 3-2 clave skips, clap on 4, galloping hats, swung 16th shaker, conga answers
grooves.notes: What the old groove missed: (1) the rim follows the 3-2 clave minus its downbeat (steps 4,7,11,13), not just 4 and 11; (2) the hats gallop (8th plus two 16ths, the 'x.xx' cell, cited by one tutorial); (3) a continuous swung 16th shaker accented on the and; (4) hand percussion answering in the gaps; (5) swing. Kick 1, and-of-2, 3 plus and-of-4 in alternating bars is audeobox's placement; beatstorapon's 'core' is 1, and-of-2, 4 with rim on 4 and 11 (the old groove). All sources are beat-level prose, none shows a grid image. Check by ear against Wizkid/Davido/P2J references.

grooves.name: afrobeats_bounce
grooves.description: afrobeats: bouncy percussion-led afropop; 3-3-2 kick, rim answering on the e and a, clap on 2 and 4, agogo bell line, rolling 16th shaker, interlocking congas and bongos
grooves.notes: Combines the 3+3+2 kick (hexloops: kicks on steps 1, 4, 7 then 9, 12, 15) with a 2-and-4 clap and a dense hand-percussion layer. The agogo figure is a generic West African bell-derived line; percussion placement is my programming, not transcribed. Thin it if it clutters.

grooves.name: afrobeats_afrofusion
grooves.description: afrobeats: slow afro-fusion / afro-R&B; soft kick on 1, the a of 2 and 3, late rim on the clave skips, snap-clap on 4, laid-back hats with ghosts, light shaker and conga
grooves.notes: beatstorapon gives ~85 BPM for sultry R&B-leaning afro tracks. Fewer hits, more lateness and swing than the main groove; the clave-skip rim keeps it afro. Pattern is my synthesis (Tems / Burna slow-jam pocket).

grooves.name: afroswing
grooves.description: afroswing: UK afroswing (J Hus, Kojo Funds); dancehall-style 3-3-2 kick, clap on 2 and 4, rim skip on the a of 2 and the and of 4, swung galloping hats and shaker
grooves.notes: beatstorapon's 'Dancehall/Afro-Swing' row has kick 1 and the a of 2 with snare on 2 and 4; most afroswing beats use the fuller 3-3-2 kick (1, 4, 7) borrowed from dancehall, which is what this uses. More swing than Naija afrobeats.

grooves.name: amapiano
grooves.description: amapiano: classic piano; soft four-on-the-floor kick, quiet clap on 2 and 4, off-beat open hat, swung 16th shaker, syncopated rim and conga clave around the log drum
grooves.notes: Roland: 909 kick on every quarter, constant 16th shaker, open hat on the off-beats, a conga clave, 112 BPM. RouteNote: 54-58% swing (about 0.12-0.24 here), claps on 2 and 4. The log drum is a bass part, not in this groove; the rim leaves the and of 1 and 3 for it. Rim and conga placement is mine.

grooves.name: amapiano_private_school
grooves.description: amapiano: private school; soft kick on 1 and 3, late rim and shaker, off-beat open hat, brushed snare ghosts, lots of space for keys and log drum
grooves.notes: Sources call private school softer, jazz-leaning, with restrained log drums and gaps for vocals, but give no grid. Kick on 1 and 3 is my reading of 'restrained'; many private-school records (Kelvin Momo) keep a soft four-on-the-floor, so this is the sparse end.

grooves.name: amapiano_bacardi
grooves.description: amapiano: bacardi / sgija; busy syncopated kick, clipped snare on 2 and 4, rattling accented 16th shaker, syncopated low and mid toms, off-beat open hat, clap pickups
grooves.notes: amapiano.co: Pretoria bacardi has syncopated kicks and toms, rattling shakers, clipped snares; sources disagree on tempo (108-113 vs 116-122) and on whether bacardi is a separate genre. Grid is my programming of the description.

grooves.name: afro_house
grooves.description: afro house: four-on-the-floor kick, clap on 2 and 4, off-beat open hat, 16th shaker, rim on the 3-2 clave, conga and bongo interplay
grooves.notes: Standard afro house layout: a house kit plus African/Latin hand percussion carrying the syncopation.

grooves.name: afro_house_tribal
grooves.description: afro house: tribal / percussive; four-on-the-floor kick, no clap, toms carrying the 3-3-2, 16th shaker, clave alternating 3-2 and 2-3, woodblock and off-beat cowbell
grooves.notes: Tom-led afro house (the percussive Keinemusik / Black Coffee side). My programming; no grid source.

grooves.name: gqom
grooves.description: gqom: Durban broken beat; no four-on-the-floor, kick on 1 and the 3-3-2 skips with gaps, heavy toms answering, snare on 3, sparse off-beat shaker, rim stabs
grooves.notes: Sources agree on the identifiers (a broken kick cycle with displaced or missing impacts, negative space, 120-130 BPM) but none shows a grid. Programmed by me; check against DJ Lag / Distruction Boyz.

grooves.name: dancehall
grooves.description: dancehall: modern bounce; kick on 1 and the a of 1 in each half bar, snare on the and of 2 and the and of 4 (together the 3-3-2), rim on 2 and 4, 8th hats, 16th shaker
grooves.notes: MusicRadar: dancehall is built on the 3-3-2 (two dotted 8ths and an 8th), split freely between kick and snare. This split (kick 1 and 4, snare 7) is a common modern one; the rim on 2 and 4 keeps a backbeat reference.

grooves.name: dancehall_steppers
grooves.description: dancehall: digital steppers; four-on-the-floor kick under a snare punching the full 3-3-2 twice a bar, closed hats around an off-beat open hat
grooves.notes: MusicRadar's example: the whole 3-3-2 punched out by the snare over a four-to-the-floor kick at 95 BPM.

grooves.name: reggae_one_drop
grooves.description: reggae one drop (triplet grid): kick and cross-stick together on beat 3 only, nothing on 1, shuffled triplet hats, hat foot on 2 and 4
grooves.notes: Carlton Barrett's one drop: beat 1 empty, kick and rim on 3. Shuffled on a triplet grid; some players use straight 8ths with swing instead.

grooves.name: dembow
grooves.description: reggaeton: dembow; kick on every beat, snare on the 3-3-2 dembow accents (soft on the a of 1, strong on the and of 2), light 8th hats
grooves.notes: Unchanged from the current library; it is the standard Dem Bow / Pounder cell.

grooves.name: reggaeton_perreo
grooves.description: reggaeton: modern perreo; four-on-the-floor kick, dembow snare with clap on the strong hits, a pickup in bar 2, accented 16th hats, open hat and timbale fill at the end of bar 2
grooves.notes: Modern perreo (Tainy / Bad Bunny era) keeps the dembow cell and adds clap layering, busier hats and bar-end pickups.

grooves.name: moombahton
grooves.description: moombahton: Dutch-house reggaeton; four-on-the-floor kick, clap on the dembow accents, rolling 16th hats, off-beat open hat, tom pickup in bar 2
grooves.notes: Moombahton: a Dutch house beat slowed to ~108 with the dembow on the clap.

grooves.name: baile_funk
grooves.description: baile funk: tamborzão (funk carioca); heavy kick cell on 1, the a of 1, the and of 2, 3 and the e of 4, conga/atabaque answers, clap on 2 and 4, dry rim
grooves.notes: Sources agree on ~130 BPM, heavy kicks, sharp snares and atabaque-style percussion in one interlocking syncopated cell, never four-on-the-floor. None gave the step grid; the kick cell (1, 4, 7, 11, 14) is my recollection of the tamborzão and needs checking by ear. The description says 'and of 3' loosely: step 11 is the and of 3.

grooves.name: baile_funk_mandelao
grooves.description: baile funk: mandelão / funk automotivo (São Paulo); fast, kick on the 3-3-2 every half bar, clap on 2 and 4, off-beat rim, cowbell stabs
grooves.notes: Sources only say mandelão / automotivo runs faster (~150) and harder. Programmed by me.

grooves.name: trap
grooves.description: trap (half-time at 130-170 BPM): sparse kicks, clap on 3, 8th hats with a 16th roll before the bar line
grooves.notes: Kick, clap and open hat unchanged. The current grooves.cpp hat lane has 32 characters per bar in a grid-4 groove (8 per beat, for the 32nd roll), which breaks the beats x grid rule; here it is the grid-4 equivalent with a 16th roll. If 32nds matter, the groove needs grid 8 (all lanes doubled) or keep the old lane if the realizer tolerates it.

grooves.name: trap_triplet
grooves.description: trap: triplet-hat flow (16th-triplet grid); kick on 1 and pushes, clap on 3, hats in 8th triplets with a 16th-triplet roll at the end of bar 2, open hat answer
grooves.notes: Migos-style triplet bounce: 6 steps per beat so hats sit on 8th-note triplets (every 2 steps) and roll on 16th triplets. Real beats switch between straight and triplet hats inside a bar, which one grid can't hold; this is the all-triplet version.

grooves.name: trap_rage
grooves.description: trap: rage (half-time); hard kick on 1 and stuttered pushes, clap on 3, snare pickup at the end of bar 2, plain 8th hats, open hat on the and of 4, crash every 2 bars
grooves.notes: Rage (Carti WLR, Ken Carson, Homixide) is driven by distorted 808s and synth leads; drums stay simple and hit hard. Programmed by me.

grooves.name: trap_plugg
grooves.description: trap: plugg / pluggnb (half-time); bouncy kick on 1, the a of 2 and the and of 3, clap on 3, 8th hats with occasional 16th doubles, rim on the a of 4, soft open hat
grooves.notes: Plugg (MexikoDro, Stoopid Lou) and pluggnb: softer, bouncier drums than trap, fewer rolls. No grid source found.
sources: (not web-sourced: programmed from the description and general producer practice)

grooves.name: trap_soul
grooves.description: trap soul (half-time): Bryson Tiller-style; sparse kick, late clap on 3, 8th hats with 16th flourishes, ghosted rim, soft shaker
grooves.notes: Trap's half-time layout with fewer kicks, a laid-back backbeat and lighter hats. Also counted at 60-75 BPM with the clap on 2 and 4; equivalent.
sources: (not web-sourced: programmed from the description and general producer practice)

grooves.name: drill
grooves.description: drill: UK drill; half-time snare on 3 then on 4 in bar 2, sliding kicks off the downbeat, tresillo hats
grooves.notes: Unchanged from the current library.

grooves.name: drill_ny
grooves.description: drill: NY / Brooklyn drill (Pop Smoke, 808Melo); half-time snare on 3 with a ghost before it and a pickup in bar 2, bouncy syncopated hats, kick on 1 and the a of 2, perc rim stabs
grooves.notes: NY drill keeps UK drill's half-time snare but uses fewer kicks (the sliding 808 carries the low end) and bouncier hats, often with triplet hat runs this grid can't hold. Programmed by me; no NY-specific grid source found.

grooves.name: phonk_drift
grooves.description: phonk: drift phonk; hard kick on 1 and the a of 2, clap on 2 and 4, driving cowbell on the 3-3-2, 16th hats, open hat on the and of 4
grooves.notes: The cowbell is the signature (in real tracks it is pitched, melodic and distorted; here only its rhythm). Sources differ on tempo (130-150 vs 140-160) and kick (four-on-the-floor or lightly syncopated); Kordhell-style drift tracks sit near 120-140 with a full-time backbeat, which is what this uses.

grooves.name: phonk_memphis
grooves.description: phonk: Memphis / classic phonk (half-time); 808 kick on 1 and pushes, clap and snare on 3, 16th 808 hats, cowbell off-beats
grooves.notes: Memphis rap tapes are counted at 65-75 BPM with the snare on 2 and 4; written half-time here to match the trap family. Programmed by me.

grooves.name: jersey_club
grooves.description: jersey club: the five-kick bounce on 1, 2, 3, the a of 3 and the and of 4; clap on 2 and 4, 8th hats, rim on the and
grooves.notes: NI: two quarter-note kicks, two dotted 8ths, an 8th = steps 1, 5, 9, 12, 15. One guide gives 1, 5, 9, 11, 13. Tempo claims range 130-160; ~140 is typical.

grooves.name: jersey_club_bounce
grooves.description: jersey club: kick-roll variant; five-kick pattern in bar 1, bar 2 rolls 1-3-5-9-11-13-15, clap on 2 and 4 with a pickup on the a of 4, 16th hats
grooves.notes: Bar 2 is beatstorapon's alternate kick (1, 5, 9, 11, 13 plus 3 and 15).

grooves.name: uk_garage
grooves.description: uk garage: 2-step; kick on 1 and the and of 3 (skipping beat 3), snare on 2 and 4, shuffled off-beat hats with ghosts, syncopated rim, swung shaker
grooves.notes: NI: snares on 2 and 4, kicks on 1 and halfway through beat 3 (step 11). Producer School: ~68% MPC swing, the most important element (mapped to 0.45 on this 0..0.5-heavy scale).

grooves.name: uk_garage_shuffle
grooves.description: uk garage: 4x4 garage shuffle; kick on 1 with soft off-beat kicks, snare on 2 and 4 with a ghost at the bar end, low clap under, swung ghosted hats and shaker
grooves.notes: Attack 'garage shuffle': kick on beat 1 plus three off-beat hits (some soft), snares on 2 and 4 plus a ghost at the bar end, a low clap under, many ghost hats, 60-65% swing, 120-125 BPM. The exact steps are in images; positions are my reading of the text.

grooves.name: uk_funky
grooves.description: uk funky: tribal syncopated kick, clap on 2 and 4, rim on the 3-3-2 skips, congas, off-beat open hat, swung 16th shaker
grooves.notes: UK funky (Crazy Cousinz, Roska, Marcus Nasty) descends from garage with soca and afro-house percussion; sources confirm the lineage but give no grid. Programmed by me.

grooves.name: jungle
grooves.description: jungle: chopped Amen break; kick on 1, the and of 1 and the and/a of 3, snares on 2 and 4 with the Amen's skipping ghosts, 8th ride, crash in bar 2
grooves.notes: Bar 1 is the Amen's main bar; bar 2 is its late-crash variation. The ride is on the break and producers usually keep it.

grooves.name: bossa_nova
grooves.description: bossa nova: cross-stick on the bossa clave over two bars, kick on 1 and 3 with pickups on the and of 2 and 4, 8th hats, hat foot on 2 and 4
grooves.notes: Standard kit bossa. The cross-stick plays the bossa clave (1, and of 2, 4 | 2, and of 3); some drummers start on the 2-side.

grooves.name: samba
grooves.description: samba: surdo kick on every beat with pickups and accents on 2 and 4, 16th ganzá shaker accented on the a, tamborim rim figure over two bars, two-tone agogo
grooves.notes: One 4/4 bar here = two 2/4 samba bars. Surdo/kick and ganzá are standard; tamborim and agogo figures vary widely between schools and these are representative, not transcribed.

grooves.name: cumbia
grooves.description: cumbia: kick on 1 and 3, guiro scraping an 8th and two 16ths, cowbell on the off-beats, conga mutes on the beat with open tones on the and of 2 and 4, cross-stick on 2 and 4
grooves.notes: Colombian/Mexican cumbia kit style; the guacharaca/guiro 'x.xx' scrape is the signature. Often notated in 2/4 at double this tempo.

grooves.name: salsa
grooves.description: salsa: son clave 2-3 (one 4/4 bar = one cut-time clave cycle); campana bell on the beats, conga tumbao with a slap and open tones on 4 and the and of 4, light kick on the bass anticipations
grooves.notes: Written at 16ths with one son clave cycle per bar, i.e. cut-time salsa at 170-210 counted as 85-105. For 3-2 swap the clave's halves ('x..x..x...x.x...'). Tumbao: heel/toe mutes, slap on 2 (accented mute), open tones on 4 and 4-and (conga then tumba).

grooves.name: rnb
grooves.description: r&b: modern R&B (SZA, Summer Walker); sparse kick on 1 and the a of 2, late snap-clap on 2 and 4, 16th hats with rolls, ghost rim, light shaker
grooves.notes: Trap-informed R&B at full time (backbeat on 2 and 4); trap_soul is the same idea counted half-time.
sources: (not web-sourced: programmed from the description and general producer practice)

grooves.name: rnb_new_jack_swing
grooves.description: r&b: 90s new jack swing; punchy kick on 1, the and of 2 and the and of 3, snare and clap on 2 and 4, heavily swung 16th hats, tambourine on 2 and 4
grooves.notes: New jack swing (Teddy Riley): drum-machine 16th swing near 66%; the swing is the genre.

grooves.name: gfunk
grooves.description: g-funk: West Coast; laid-back kick on 1, the a of 2 and 3, snare and clap on 2 and 4, accented 16th hats, 8th shaker, open hat on the and of 4
grooves.notes: Dr. Dre / DJ Quik era programmed drums (808-ish kit, live-funk feel). Common practice, not a transcription.

grooves.name: disco
grooves.description: disco: four-on-the-floor kick, snare on 2 and 4, open hat on every off-beat with closed hats around it, tambourine on 2 and 4
grooves.notes: Classic disco kit.
